message: Forest finished: its small accessors are #[inline] (build level with the arena at 10k and ~10% faster at 100k, measured alone; link walks a fifth faster), move_to builds its refusal messages out of line and skips the ancestor walk for a reorder. Reordering stays behind the arena on short lists only, by the id and cycle checks, and wins from a few hundred children; the speed rule now says so, and Forest is done. (proposal 01a15b7a-b436-775a-8ae7-aa3bf081eee9, proposed by agent:claude-code, accepted by user)

text: At least as fast as a hand-written arena of the same shape (build, remove a subtree, full preorder at 10,000 and 100,000 nodes, a dirty walk with 1% dirty), and reordering children takes the same time whatever the list's length, checked by benchmarks run one at a time.

reason: The build gap it was for closed with #[inline]: building measures level with the arena at 10k (69 against 68 us) and ~10% faster at 100k (0.98 against 1.1 ms), each run alone. parda can ask for it if reconciliation shows a need.

title: The forest's small accessors are #[inline]
body: Benchmarks (and parda) call the forest from another crate, where a non-generic function isn't inlined without #[inline]: every check, id and link step was a call. With #[inline] on 38 small functions, building fell from 75 to 34 us at 10k and 1.07 to 0.63 ms at 100k (same order and warm memory), and link preorder from 182 to 145 us at 100k. Run alone, building measures 69 us / 0.98 ms against the arena's 68 us / 1.1 ms: the forest allocates its slots up front, and faulting in fresh pages dominates a cold run. So compare benchmarks run one at a time; a run right after another that freed memory reads up to twice as fast.

title: Reordering is constant-time; the arena wins only on short lists
body: move_to builds its refusal messages in a cold function and skips the ancestor walk when the node stays under its parent (it can't be inside its own subtree): 10.1 to 9.8 ns, little, because what's left is the id checks and relinking up to five records. benches/forest.rs reorder_wide: the forest takes about 9 ns at 16, 256 and 4096 children; the arena's Vec shift takes 4.4, 14 and 204 ns. Matching the arena on 16 children would mean dropping the checks that make a stale id fail safely, so the rule now asks for constant time instead.
